name: UG Brighton | Meetup #17 - Once Upon Agentic AI
description:
Join us for Meetup #17 of the AWS Brighton User Group, where you will get hands-on building AI agents using Strands (https://strandsagents.com/) - the open-source Python framework from AWS for creating agents that can reason, use tools, and work together.

Bring your laptop to follow along with the workshop, which takes you on a progressive quest from summoning your first AI agent through to orchestrating multi-agent systems.

You will learn how to create and configure agents, equip them with built-in and custom tools, connect to external services via Model Context Protocol (MCP), and build Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication patterns.

This workshop is accessible for anyone with basic Python knowledge. You can read up about the workshop ahead of time here (https://catalog.us-east-1.prod.workshops.aws/workshops/e1493217-4bc7-42f4-87d9-e231acd743bc/en-US).

Don't fancy getting hands-on? Pop along anyway and network, and learn about AI agents on AWS.

Don't have a laptop you can bring? We will team you up with someone who does, and should have a couple of "spares" too.

No need to have an AWS account - we'll set you up with a sandbox environment so you don't have to worry about the AWS bill either. You will need an AWS Builder ID to access the sandbox environment, which you can set up here (https://aws.amazon.com/builder/), or we can help you during the workshop.

name: AWS Women in Tech: Fireside Chat Series with Uma Boddeti
description:
AI is changing quickly, but building a career in technology still comes back to strong fundamentals, curiosity, and a willingness to keep learning. 

Join Uma, Director of Engineering for AI Foundations at AWS Applied AI Solutions, for a conversation about building a long-term technical career and growing with the technology around you. With more than 20 years of experience across Amazon, AWS, and Google, Uma has worked across cloud architecture, large-scale systems, and now generative and agentic AI. She will share lessons from her career, how she has continued to grow as an engineer and leader, and what students can focus on today as they prepare for a future shaped by AI. 

About the speaker: 

Uma Boddeti is Director of Engineering for AI Foundations at AWS Applied AI Solutions, where she serves as Platform Lead for Mosaic, an enterprise AI infrastructure and governance platform for multi-agent systems. She has more than 20 years of experience across Amazon, AWS, and Google, with expertise in cloud architecture, large-scale distributed systems, and generative and agentic AI. Outside of work, she is a mother of two who enjoys traveling, hiking, classical dance, and baking.

 

Note: The AWS Women in Tech: Fireside Chat Series is open to all. Whether you’re interested in building technical skills, learning from AWS leaders, or exploring career opportunities, you’re welcome to join.

name: AWS Women in Tech: Fireside Chat Series with Kathy Kam
description:
What does it take to build a long-term career in engineering while technology keeps changing?

Join Kathy Kam, who leads engineering for Kiro at AWS, for a conversation about growing as an engineer, taking on leadership opportunities, and adapting to new technology. With 25 years of experience building developer platforms, Kathy has worked on everything from foundational web technologies to cloud services and AI-powered developer tools.

Note: The AWS Women in Tech: Fireside Chat Series is open to all. Whether you’re interested in building technical skills, learning from AWS leaders, or exploring career opportunities, you’re welcome to join.

description:

name: AWS Women in Tech: Fireside Chat Series with Laura Grit
description:
Building a long-term technical career is not just about keeping up with new technology. It is also about learning how to solve bigger problems, influence others, and grow as a leader.

Join Laura Grit, Vice President and Distinguished Engineer at AWS, for a conversation about technical leadership, building confidence, and growing a career while technology continues to change. Laura has worked on some of Amazon’s largest technology transformations, including helping move Amazon.com from on-premises data centers to AWS services, and today she is helping drive AI transformation within AWS. She will share what she has learned about leading without always having formal authority, developing technical depth, and creating opportunities for the next generation of engineers.

Laura Grit is a Vice President and Distinguished Engineer at AWS, specializing in cloud infrastructure efficiency, large-scale cloud migration, resiliency, and developer productivity. Since joining Amazon in 2007, she has helped lead major technical initiatives, served as Technical Advisor to the AWS CEO, and is now helping drive AI transformation within AWS. Laura is also a strong advocate for developing technical leaders and has supported women in engineering and the Amazon Principal Engineer community.

name: Halloween en la Nube: nada da más miedo que un outage
description:
Esta noche de Halloween no le tememos a los fantasmas. Le tememos al outage.

En el AWS User Group Santa Cruz de la Sierra te invitamos a “Halloween en la Nube”, una edición especial para hablar de lo que de verdad asusta cuando trabajas en AWS: caídas en producción, funciones Lambda que fallan en silencio, bases de datos que no responden, deploys de viernes que rompen todo y facturas que aparecen como espectros a fin de mes.

Y como todo buen relato de terror, también vamos a ver cómo sobrevivir: arquitecturas resilientes, monitoreo, seguridad y buenas prácticas para que tus servicios no tengan que salir corriendo.

name: AWS Level up: 5 Techniques to Stop AI Agent Hallucinations
description:
AI agents can make mistakes in different ways, from pulling the wrong information to choosing the wrong tool or saying a task was completed when it was not.

In this hands-on workshop, you’ll explore five practical techniques for making AI agents more reliable. Using a travel booking agent as the example, you’ll see how approaches like Graph-RAG, semantic tool selection, guardrails, runtime steering, and multi-agent validation can help reduce different types of hallucinations.

You’ll leave with reusable patterns and a better understanding of which approach to use depending on the problem you are trying to solve.

Presenters: Elizabeth Fuentes Leone, Laura Salinas and Sandhya Subramani

name: Hands-on Workshop: Strands Agents
description:
¡Hola, comunidad de AWS UG Chiclayo! 👋

En este meetup nos meteremos de lleno en el taller práctico "Getting Started with Strands Agents" 🤖✨

Este espacio está diseñado para avanzar paso a paso de forma totalmente _hands-on_, aprendiendo a construir y ejecutar agentes de IA con solo unas pocas líneas de código. Utilizaremos Strands Agents, un SDK open source que simplifica la complejidad del desarrollo, permitiéndote conectar modelos (como Amazon Nova o Anthropic Claude) y herramientas de forma rápida y eficiente.

📍 REQUISITO IMPORTANTE PARA EL ACCESO: Para asegurar tu ingreso a las instalaciones de la USAT (Laboratorio de software 1), es indispensable que completes el siguiente formulario de registro con tus datos: 👉 Link de Registro (https://awsugchiclayo.com/registro/getting-started-strands-agents-part-2/)

¿Qué revisaremos en esta sesión?

* Conceptos Core y el Agentic Loop: Entenderemos cómo interactúan el modelo, las herramientas y el prompt para que el agente razone, planifique y complete tareas de manera autónoma.
* Integración Flexible de Herramientas: Aprenderemos a usar herramientas integradas, a convertir cualquier función de Python en una herramienta personalizada usando decoradores, y a conectar servicios externos mediante el estándar MCP.
* Soporte Multi-Modelo: Veremos cómo cambiar fácilmente entre diferentes proveedores de LLMs en Amazon Bedrock (y otros entornos) para elegir el modelo ideal según el caso de uso.
* Arquitecturas Multi-Agente Avanzadas: Exploraremos cómo hacer que múltiples agentes colaboren para resolver problemas complejos usando patrones como _Agent as Tool_, _Swarm_, _Graph_ y _Workflow_.
* Capacidades Enterprise: Revisaremos cómo implementar observabilidad y trazabilidad distribuida (tracing) usando OpenTelemetry (OTEL) para monitorear nuestras sesiones.

🎯 ¿Para quién es este evento? Este evento está diseñado para estudiantes, entusiastas de la tecnología, desarrolladores y arquitectos de software que quieran dar el salto de la teoría a la práctica y aprender a construir aplicaciones de IA modernas. ¡No necesitas experiencia previa avanzada, solo ganas de aprender y explorar el ecosistema cloud!

💻 Nota importante: El workshop se desarrollará en un laboratorio equipado, por lo que no es necesario que traigas tu laptop. ¡Solo ven listo para aprender y programar!

name: Architecting for Trust: Resilience & Sovereignty on AWS
description:
Join us for an evening focused on building trusted cloud architectures — featuring a hands-on resilience workshop, expert talks from AWS, and time to connect with the
community. We’ll explore how organizations can design cloud systems that are resilient, reliable, and sovereign, from implementing resilience patterns on AWS to understanding the difference between resilience and sovereignty in modern cloud architectures. You can join the hands-on workshop, the talk sessions, or — even better — both!

Sign up for free on our Meetup Page (https://copeb.it/3SC74W)

Hands-on Lab:

In this afternoon workshop, guided by AWS architects, you'll work hands-on with Karpenter, the open-source autoscaler for Kubernetes. Resilience starts with capacity: if your cluster can't scale when demand changes, your applications can't stay available. You'll see how Karpenter automatically provisions just the right compute resources for your cluster's applications, and how to define and manage your autoscaling policies with NodePools. The right nodes at the right time: you work through real scenarios on your own laptop. Based on AWS Workshop Studio.
Please bring your laptop!

Talks + Speakers

Design Resilient Workloads on AWS (Michael Schmid)

To deal with unexpected events, you have to design your workloads to be resilient. To address this, AWS has developed the Resilience Lifecylce Framework. In this session we will review Resilient Software Design Patterns for building resilient applications, such as graceful degradation, static stability, exponential backoff, and circuit breakers.

Enterprise Claude Code, Built Natively on AWS (Roman Frei)

In this talk, Roman Frei, Product Owner at copebit AG, explains how his team built a private backend that lets engineers use AI coding tools like Claude Code while keeping enterprises compliant, guaranteeing EU data residency, full audit trails, and governance, all built entirely with native AWS services.

Digital Sovereignty - Facts beyond the hype (Dani Caduff)

In this talk, Daniel Caduff, Principal Security Assurance DACH at AWS, explains the difference between resilience and sovereignty in modern cloud architectures.

About copebit AG

copebit AG is a Swiss cloud consulting and engineering company focused on transparency, innovation, and long-term partnerships.
With deep expertise in AWS and modern DevOps practices, Copebit helps organizations design, build, and operate secure, scalable cloud solutions.

description:
Agentic Software Delivery: A Fireside Chat with AWS DevEx Researchers

As AI reshapes how software gets built, developers and leaders face a new set of questions. How do teams use tokens most efficiently and keep AI costs stable? How can teams best address new bottlenecks, like code review? And what are the emerging practices for building software factories and a true AI-native SDLC?

Join Laura Tacho and Nathen Harvey, two industry experts on developer productivity, for a candid fireside conversation grounded in their latest work. They'll dig into the data on what is really helping orgs win with AI, share trends and insights about tokenomics, ROI, and new bottlenecks, and offer their take on where agentic development is headed. Expect a frank discussion on what works and how to measure it, from DORA metrics to developer-level signals, and plenty of time for Q&A.

Agenda

18:30 - 19:30 Doors open for networking, food, and drinks

19:30 - 20:30 Fireside Chat with Laura and Nathen

20:30 - 21:00 Closing Remarks & Networking

Speakers

Laura Tacho (https://www.linkedin.com/in/lauratacho/)  
Laura is an expert in developer experience and measuring the efficiency of engineering organizations. She currently works on developer experience at AWS, and was previously the CTO of DX, where she led the company's research and advisory practices, helping engineering leaders make better decisions about how and when to invest in devex, platform tooling, and AI. Laura's been working on developer tools for 15 years, including building out some of the first developer tools for the Docker ecosystem, and then on CI/CD and automation tools. In 2021, she started her own executive advisory practice and has worked with over 1500 engineering leaders on developer experience, measuring productivity, and creating high-performing engineering orgs.

Nathen Harvey (https://www.linkedin.com/in/nathen/)  
Nathen is a Principal Technologist on the Developer Experience team at AWS, focusing on software delivery performance, platform engineering, and AI enablement. He previously led DORA at Google Cloud, guiding the industry-standard framework for measuring engineering performance. As the lead author of multiple DORA reports and a former Vice President at Chef, Nathen brings deep expertise in shaping developer ecosystems. He is a frequent keynote speaker, a co-founder of regional DevOpsDays events, and a co-author of 97 Things Every Cloud Engineer Should Know.

name: UG Genova | Once Upon Agentic AI
description:
Once Upon Agentic AI è un workshop hands-on, a tema RPG, pensato per imparare i concetti fondamentali di Strands Agents costruendo passo dopo passo un Game Master per Dungeons & Dragons basato su agenti AI.

Partiremo dalla creazione di un singolo agente e ne estenderemo progressivamente le capacità: svilupperemo tool personalizzati, integreremo un server MCP (Model Context Protocol), introdurremo la comunicazione tra agenti tramite Agent-to-Agent (A2A) e costruiremo una interfaccia web per interagire con il sistema. Infine, ricostruiremo la stessa soluzione utilizzando Strands Harness, per vedere come cambia l’approccio allo sviluppo e all’orchestrazione.

Attraverso un progetto concreto, divertente e progressivo, esploreremo i principali building block dei sistemi agentici moderni e i pattern necessari per creare agenti, dotarli di strumenti e farli collaborare tra loro.

Al termine del workshop avrai sia le competenze pratiche sia i materiali necessari per poter riproporre l’esperienza in autonomia nella tua community.
